translationRepairs: Supreme commander Wang Duo, by imperial order, made Wen grand general of the Left Golden Guard and deputy campaign commander in Hezhong. The court then gave him the name Quanzhong—"wholly loyal."

Supreme commander Wang Duo, by imperial order, made Wen grand general of the Left Golden Guard and deputy campaign commander in Hezhong. The Son of Heaven then gave Wen the name Quanzhong—"wholly loyal."
Restores the explicitly named imperial actor and Zhu Wen in the grant of his new name.
In the ninth month the court named Quanzhong honorary privy councilor and made him Marquis of Pei.
In the ninth month the Son of Heaven appointed Quanzhong acting Situ and chancellor, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pei.
Restores the sovereign and both offices without importing an inaccurate English expansion for 檢校司徒.
"Shi Pu of Xuzhou": whenever the text identifies someone as "so-and-so of such-and-such prefecture," it means the military governor of that prefecture.
As for Shi Pu of Xuzhou: whenever the text identifies someone as "so-and-so of such-and-such prefecture," it means the military governor of that prefecture.
The source is a continuous explanatory note, not a quoted lemma.
Quanzhong's forces were too weak to risk a sortie.
The Prince had few troops and did not dare to sally out.
Preserves the staged princely title and the direct statement while reading naturally in English.
In the tenth month the court sent a monument commemorating his victories.
In the tenth month the Son of Heaven sent an envoy and bestowed on the Prince a stele commemorating his victories.
Restores both the envoy and the Prince omitted by the former idiomatic version.
Xian held Banqiao, Zhi the north suburbs, Tang Wansheng—thirty-six camps encircling Bian.
Xian camped at Banqiao, Zhi at the northern suburbs, and Tang at Wansheng; they ringed Bian with thirty-six stockades.
Separates Lu Tang from Wansheng, where his army was stationed.
In the tenth month the court gave Quanzhong the Xuanyi command as well. He marched to Huazhou, crossed Wei to strike Hedong, and demanded grain from the Wei garrison—partly to pick a fight.

In the tenth month the Son of Heaven gave the Prince the Xuanyi command as well. He marched to Huazhou, asked passage through Wei to strike Hedong, and demanded military supplies, thereby provoking Wei and creating a pretext for war.
Restores the sovereign, princely title, requested passage, military requisition, and stated purpose without the unnecessary Latinism.
Zhao Kuangning of Xiangzhou had been a vassal since his father Dezhao's day. He was now in touch with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the traffic was discovered.
Zhao Kuangning of Xiangzhou had been a vassal since his father Deyin's day. He was now in touch with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the traffic was discovered.
Corrects Zhao Kuangning's father's name to the source spelling.
Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture had submitted since his father Dezhao's time; Kuangning again communicated with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the matter was exposed.
Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture had submitted since his father Deyin's time; Kuangning again communicated with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the matter was exposed.
Corrects Zhao Kuangning's father's name to the source spelling in the literal field as well.
Shi Shucung came through the Taihang and captured Zezhou and Luzhou.
Shi Shuzong came through the Taihang and captured Zezhou and Luzhou.
Corrects the established romanization of 氏叔琮.
Shi Shucung went out through the Taihang and took Ze and Lu.
Shi Shuzong went out through the Taihang and took Ze and Lu.
Corrects the established romanization of 氏叔琮 in the literal field as well.

In the first month of Tainyou 1 (904) Quanzhong went to Hezhong and sent his gate officer Kou Yanqing to Chang'an to demand the move to Luoyang and the resettlement of the western capital's population.

In the first month of Tianyou 1 (904) Quanzhong went to Hezhong and sent his gate officer Kou Yanqing to Chang'an to demand the move to Luoyang and the resettlement of the western capital's population.
Corrects the reign-name romanization in the idiomatic field.
